findings.reason: a worker must either encode four fields and drop an enumerated value or carry five against a done-when that says four, so the section's own measure is unsatisfiable as written.
findings.text: §2's done-when asserts the start row carries "the four fields" while the deliverable at line 42 enumerates five values (run id, node, lane, model, time budget), so the measure cannot be written unambiguously and a node may implement or test a row missing one of the named fields

findings.reason: naming `DISPLAY_HUE` (and the classifier vocabulary) as part of what the seven-word table reconciles is the difference between the pane resolving a hue for every new word and it dropping every row to the dim fallback.
findings.text: §5 says the mapping is "owned in one place" and retires `DISPLAY`, but colour for the seven words is resolved by `DISPLAY_HUE` (reckon/crew/ticker.py:195, read at :897) keyed on the old alias words, and the section's done-when checks only that words come from the set, never that they render in-colour, so retiring `DISPLAY` alone leaves the new words rendering dim and §5's single-owner claim false
